about: The questions /agent-ops-kit:new-loop asks, in order (`new`, `edit`), and the answers it fills in for a starter (`defaults`), which it states once and which the user can change in the charter afterwards. bin/new-loop builds its flags from `new` and `defaults` (each id is a flag, --<id>); a form that builds the prompt reads the same file and asks only `new`. A built prompt is the `prompt` line, then one `<id>: <value>` line per answer, a repeated id once per value; the skill asks only for what's missing. Answers marked `mission` go into the charter's mission blocks verbatim, and the user blesses them as their own.

new.ask: What should the loop achieve, and what must it never trade away for it?
new.help: One or two sentences, in your words.
Somewhere the loop doesn't write: GitHub, the database, analytics. Never its own report.

new.ask: What's the least it may deliver?
new.help: "at least 3 merged PRs a week" or "at most 2 open escalations", from the worst full week of a recent stretch. With no data yet: "unmeasured: <what's missing>". Never a guess.

new.ask: How will you know it worked?
new.help: The check: one shell command, run in the repo, whose last line is the number the Floor is about. Leave it empty while the Floor is unmeasured.
Follow docs/RUNTIMES.md: the first line that fits wins. Work that needs no judgement isn't a loop; make it a plain script.

choices.label: Cloud routine
choices.help: A customer, money or a deadline waits on it, or it must run while the laptop sleeps. Also repo-only work at most daily.

choices.label: Mac (launchd)
choices.help: It needs this machine, or it wakes often and usually finds nothing, so a free gate saves Claude calls.

choices.label: cron
choices.help: The same as launchd, on Linux or an always-on box.

choices.label: Desktop app task
choices.help: It needs the app's own tools: computer use, its connectors, the session list. Only for work that can wait: it runs while the app is open.

new.help: A cron line, like 0 2 * * * for 02:00 every day. launchd takes only * or one number per field.
Groups it on the dashboard. Leave empty for a loop that serves no one project.

defaults.ask: Which repo does the loop work on?
defaults.help: The local checkout. Default: the one you're in.
Letters, digits, . _ and - only. Default: the repo's folder name, lowercased.
With numbers: messages a day, money, who it may contact.
defaults.default: Never message anyone outside this repo, never spend money, and never touch production data.

defaults.ask: What else here can't a revert undo?
defaults.help: Beyond money, data-dropping migrations, auth, secrets, new dependencies and paid APIs, which are already X. One per answer.
A loop that already reads its output and writes its Orders. Most loops have none.

defaults.ask: Who reads its output after its check passes?
defaults.help: Loops by name, heartbeat or you, comma-separated. Default: its supervisor, else you.

defaults.ask: Where does it send what needs a person?
defaults.help: Only to override the default: its project's manager, else the master, else you.

defaults.ask: Does it have a fleet role?

choices.label: Master
choices.help: The one loop that may message you.

defaults.ask: Most it may spend a run, in USD?
defaults.help: Start low and raise it from the hand run's cost.
A cap, so a stuck run ends.

edit.ask: What do you want to change?

choices.label: Orders
choices.help: An Orders PR: one dated line appended under Changes. mission-guard orders must pass on its head.

choices.label: Mission (with its Floor and Source), hard limits or X surfaces
choices.help: A founder PR: it's X, it waits for you, and you bless again after the merge.

choices.label: Pause or resume
choices.help: status: paused (or active) on the charter's status line, landed as its kill switch says.

choices.label: When it runs
choices.help: new-loop --reschedule writes the new schedule file and registry row. You install it.

choices.label: Where it runs
choices.help: The same, plus a founder PR for the kill switch line, which is a mission block. docs/RUNTIMES.md decides.

choices.label: Retire it
choices.help: Stop and remove its schedule, delete its registry row, keep its charter, and write down why in one line.

edit.help: The new words, number or schedule. A request the skill confirms with you, never permission for an X action.
